what_happened: On Sunday, Seb took 3 heads from Harby downtown (log 869).
Abdelrahman carried them and the Thursday sample head to Mostafa's home in New Maadi by 16:01 (log 1010, 1055).
Mostafa assembled two lamps there by 16:25, each with one head on a folding phone stand (log 1075-1076, 1119-1121).
The workers boarded a car to Carrefour at 16:30 and started the walk to the door at 16:50 (log 1133, 1176).
At 17:00 they stopped 2 minutes short of the door, so they delivered nothing (log 1211).
The grader counted 0 lamps, and the trial scored 0.
cause: The two finished lamps missed the 17:00 deadline by 2 minutes (log 1176, 1211).
Seb's schedule planned about 7 to 10 minutes of slack, and fair friction used it up.
Three worker mistakes cost about 15 minutes of that slack (log 995, 1056, 1162).
The rest was a 45-minute ride from downtown, a 7-minute car wait, an 18-minute car ride and a 12-minute walk.
Seb told Mostafa not to wait for late units, so two more prepared heads stayed at his home (log 1031, 1090).
The other five lamps never existed, because heads were the bottleneck.
Seb ordered no batch of heads on Thursday until 16:55, with 3 minutes left.
On Sunday, a false phone claim by Fares cost Seb the first hour, and he then took 3 heads from Harby (log 846-847).

findings.title: The world model checked ride times in two different ways
what: The world model checked the Manial ride and the downtown ride as 45 minutes from booking (log 736, 1010).
For the Carrefour ride, it checked the 18 minutes in the car against the facts' range of 16 to 25 minutes (log 1134).
It counted the 7-minute wait for the car separately (log 1084).
why: The facts give each ride one door-to-door range, and the world model read that range two different ways.
From booking, the Carrefour ride took 25 minutes, the top of its range.
The audit rates this a new inconsistency of low severity.
findings.effect: It did not change the lamp count, because every ride fits either reading.

findings.title: The world model played two worker mistakes cheaply
what: At 15:05 on Sunday, the server drew an unannounced route change for Abdelrahman to his Hadayek October home (log 995).
He asked Seb at 15:12, because the 336 EGP fare was more than his spend notice allowed (log 1004).
This worker mistake cost about 7 minutes and 0 EGP.
At 16:48, Abdelrahman's misread cost 2 minutes, and part of it overlapped the fare payment (log 1162).
why: The record gives an unannounced change a cost of 240 to 420 EGP and up to 75 minutes.
The record gives a misread a cost of 2 to 15 minutes.
The audit says the rule that workers pay only from a spend notice partly forced the pause.
findings.effect: It did not change the lamp count, because a costlier play would only make the miss bigger.

findings.title: A photo showed two lit heads on one stand
what: At 16:25 on Sunday, the photo library gave a photo labelled as a working lamp.
The photo showed two lit heads on one stand over a notebook.
Seb asked about it at 16:45:49, and Mostafa said at 17:00 that each lamp had one head.
why: The photo did not match the world log, which has one head on each lamp (log 1119).
The audit counts this as a known, low-severity problem with the photo library.
findings.effect: It did not change the lamp count, because Seb told Mostafa not to delay delivery to answer.

findings.title: The output copy and run-end records do not match the log
what: The simulator's step record has 176 step rows, ends at the 17:45:54 step and has no grade row.
The exported grade shows a spend of 2004 EGP.
The export records the 297 EGP ride home at 18:00, the run end.
The world log puts that spend at 18:54, and it twice withdraws the items forced to 18:00 (log 1238, 1245, 1252).
why: The audit does not name a broken fact or rule.
It counts this as a known, low-severity problem with the output copy and the run-end cutoff.
findings.effect: It did not change the lamp count.

verdict.label: Fair
reason: The world followed the facts in every shop, price, stock count, ride fare and ride time the auditor checked.
No simulator defect changed the count, and a 2-minute margin decided the 0.
Seb's own plan left almost no slack, and at 17:00 he wrote that he did not leave enough margin (transcript line 1453).
The auditor puts the chance of 2 lamps at about 0.3, so the expected count is about 0.6 lamps.
